boundary: Pinned linux/amd64 64-bit validation target: int/uint are 64-bit and distinct from int64/uint64; no other OS or architecture is validated.
reason: One pinned target lets the Admissible-equals-go-build adequacy target be differentially attacked against one real toolchain, and lets int/uint be concrete types with complete proof surfaces, instead of a target-parametric width threaded through every numeric proof.
enforcement: Integer.v; Makefile PLATFORM; Dockerfile go-e2e GOOS/GOARCH guards; digest-pinned golang:1.23-alpine.
reopen_trigger: 32-bit, arm64 or another OS; any portable-Go public claim; uintptr or layout work; a toolchain image change.

boundary: Platform filesystem and resource limits are not modelled: NAME_MAX, PATH_MAX, inode, disk and memory ceilings. Paths are arbitrary length with no numeric cap.
reason: These limits are platform-specific and outside the Go-source and cmd/go semantic domain. An over-long path fails loud at the OS during materialization, never silently in the model or the grammar.
enforcement: FilePath.v and ModulePath.v carry no length cap; materialization surfaces ENAMETOOLONG.
reopen_trigger: A decision to model a specific deployment filesystem as a semantic domain.

boundary: Cooperating-developer threat boundary: the publication path is not hardened against a deliberate local bypass or against tampering with its own verifier.
reason: The enforced property is that published bytes were validated by a pinned build, for a cooperating developer using ordinary Git. Resisting a local adversary would need a different mechanism and is not claimed.
enforcement: Docker validate-before-publish stage graph; pre-commit hook over the staged index; go build ./... gating the sync image.
reopen_trigger: A decision to make publication resistant to deliberate local bypass, or a server-side CI boundary.

boundary: Host Rocq and OCaml builds are unsupported. Everything runs through pinned Buildx containers.
reason: A pinned container is the only reproducible version-exact toolchain. A host install is a second unpinned authority for the same facts.
enforcement: Makefile routes every target through buildx; Dockerfile pins every base image and package.
reopen_trigger: A decision to support and pin a host toolchain as an equal authority.

boundary: Module-path grammar exclusions: every Go-valid module path outside the narrow canonical grammar, including /vN suffixes and gopkg.in forms.
reason: The module path is a semantic fact rendered into go.mod. A deliberately narrow one-way grammar makes invalid paths unrepresentable rather than rejected, and excludes the two Go 1.23 semantic-import-versioning classes exactly.
enforcement: ModulePath.v segment grammar; representable and unrepresentable fixtures.
reopen_trigger: Imports or multi-module support needing an excluded form.

boundary: Source-file naming restrictions: (a) hidden, _test.go, testdata and vendor paths; (b) every valid Go source path outside lowercase-ASCII canonical form.
reason: (a) faithfulness to go build file selection; (b) a canonical decidable minimal path domain with no case-folding or collision questions.
enforcement: FilePath.v component_ok, reserved_dir, filename_ok, path_ok and their fixtures.
reopen_trigger: A need to represent a valid mixed-case, hyphen or underscore Go source path.

boundary: Imports on hold: no import syntax is representable and every file has an intrinsically empty import section.
reason: The closed-world guarantee requires Admissible to resolve every import to a package owned by the same program, or reject the whole program. Nothing may resolve to stdlib, cache, network, vendor, workspace or ambient filesystem.
enforcement: Syntax.imports has no constructors, so imports are unrepresentable rather than rejected.
reopen_trigger: The imports arc landing with its resolver and closed-world proof, under explicit sign-off.

boundary: Unrepresented Go syntax: the admitted fragment is println of primitive literals plus one source-shaped explicit conversion naming one of sixteen source type names.
reason: The certified fragment stays small and grows only by proof principles, never by lists of examples. A construct that cannot be modelled exactly is removed from the AST rather than admitted with a conservative narrowing.
enforcement: Syntax carries only the fragment constructors; Names carries the closed sixteen-name class.
reopen_trigger: Each future checkpoint landing a new construct with complete Admissible, Property, Render and differential obligations.

boundary: Bounded Float.Decimal literal domain: canonical coeff times 10^exp with abs(coeff) below 10^40 and abs(exp10) at most 4096.
reason: A pre-existing Float.v bound whose justification was never recorded. It is narrower than Go float constants and its minimality is not established.
enforcement: Float.v decimal_max_coeff, decimal_max_exp and the canonicality bounds.
reopen_trigger: Any real float literal beyond the box; a decision to match Go float-constant precision; ADR-0002 being reopened.

boundary: C6 operand names may not spell `main`. Go permits both the package `main` function as a value and a recursive `main()` call; under the one application root a head is an operand, so neither form is representable in C6.
reason: C6 has no function type and no function value. Admitting the operand would make valid Go representable and then rejected, violating exact admissibility. Unrepresentable is the honest boundary.
enforcement: Syntax.OperandIdentifier carries proof its spelling is not "main"; GRAM-104 records the admitted subset.
reopen_trigger: The functions milestone landing function types and values, which pays this price in full.

boundary: C6 names may not spell `any`, `comparable`, `error` or `uintptr` in an operand or a type use. Valid Go uses of those types, including conversions written through the one application root, are unrepresentable in C6.
reason: C6 implements none of them. A raw ordinary identifier in a type use would make valid programs representable and then rejected. A user declaration may still bind these spellings; only the C6 type-use source form is restricted, which also gives up their shadowed uses until the full roots land.
enforcement: Syntax.OperandIdentifier and Syntax.TypeIdentifier each carry proof the spelling is outside that set.
reopen_trigger: Interfaces for `any`, `comparable` and `error`; the priced `uintptr` target decision for `uintptr`.
